title: Subject and sample QC columns collide in the joined sample table
description:
A cohort can hold a QC flag on a subject and on a sample. Both use the columns `qc_status` and `qc_reason`, so the joined table gets `.x` and `.y` names and has no `qc_status` column.

```r
cohort <- cohort_qc(cohort, "R1", scope = "subject", action = "flag", reason = "consent under review")
cohort <- cohort_qc(cohort, "B2", scope = "sample", action = "flag", reason = "low depth")

names(samples(cohort, with_subjects = TRUE))
#> [1] "subject_id"  "assay"       "sample_id"   "role"        "qc_status.x"
#> [6] "qc_reason.x" "species"     "qc_status.y" "qc_reason.y"
```

`as_coldata()` returns the same names.

Expected: names that say the level, for example `subject_qc_status` for the flag of the subject.

biocohort 0.1.1, R 4.6.1, Windows 11

title: Combine two cohorts with a table that links their subject ids
description:
No function joins two cohorts. Two data sets of the same people often use different subject ids, for example the ids of a sequencing core and the study codes of a clinic.

Proposal:

```r
links <- data.frame(
  cohort = c("seq", "seq", "clinic", "clinic"),
  from = c("R1", "R2", "C7", "C9"),
  subject_id = c("P1", "P2", "P1", "P2")
)
both <- cohort_bind(seq = cohort_seq, clinic = cohort_clinic, links = links)
```

With `links = NULL` the cohorts already share their ids. The QC log, the derive log and the registered analyses of both cohorts stay in the result.

title: Load large analysis tables without reading them into memory
description:
`load_analysis()` reads every file in full and binds the rows into one tibble. That does not work for a table that is larger than the memory, such as variant calls or single cell values.

```r
spec <- analysis_spec_new(
  name = "variants", assay = "wgs", level = "cohort",
  path_template = "{root}/variants", root_key = "wgs_root",
  format = "parquet", reader = "arrow::open_dataset"
)
class(load_analysis(cohort, spec)$data)
#> [1] "tbl_df"     "tbl"        "data.frame"
```

The reader returns an arrow Dataset, and `load_analysis()` turns it into a tibble with every row.

Proposal: `load_analysis(cohort, spec, lazy = TRUE)` returns the object of the reader as it is. A format `parquet_dataset` with `arrow::open_dataset` as its reader covers a partitioned folder.

title: Add a column dictionary with types, labels, units and allowed values
description:
Every manifest column is text. That is right for ids. For a value such as age, each script converts the type again, and each plot needs a label and a unit that the cohort does not hold.

```r
sapply(subjects(cohort), class)
#>  subject_id     species         age
#> "character" "character" "character"
```

Proposal: an optional dictionary with the type, the label, the unit and the allowed values of each column.

```r
dictionary <- data.frame(
  column = c("age", "sex"),
  type = c("number", "string"),
  label = c("Age at enrollment", "Sex"),
  unit = c("years", NA),
  values = c(NA, "F|M")
)
cohort <- cohort_new(subject_tbl, sample_map, dictionary = dictionary)
subjects(cohort, typed = TRUE)
```

The stored tables stay text, so the id checks do not change.

title: Read several manifest files into one cohort
description:
`read_manifest()` takes one file. A study with several assays often has one sample sheet per assay.

```r
read_manifest(c("rna_samples.csv", "proteomics_samples.csv"))
#> Error: Assertion on 'path' failed: Must have length 1.
```

Stacking the sheets by hand also fails when one sheet lacks a column, because a missing value next to a given value counts as a conflict.

```r
manifest <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("R1", "R1"), species = "human", sex = c("F", NA),
  assay = c("bulk_rna", "proteomics"), sample_id = c("A1", "P1")
)
validate_manifest(manifest)
#> Error: `manifest` has conflicting subject-level metadata.
#> Subject and column that vary: R1 (sex).
```

Proposal: `read_manifest()` accepts several paths and stacks them before validation. A missing value is no conflict, and the given value fills the subject row.

title: Keep the QC, derive and corrections logs in the study YAML round trip
description:
A cohort that is written with `write_study_yaml()` and read back has empty logs. The reason, the time and the cutoffs of each action are lost.

```r
c(nrow(qc_log(cohort)), nrow(derive_log(cohort)))
#> [1] 1 1

write_study_yaml(cohort, "study.yaml")
back <- read_study_yaml("study.yaml")
c(nrow(qc_log(back)), nrow(derive_log(back)))
#> [1] 0 0
```

`corrections_log()` has the same gap. It returns an empty table for a cohort that was built from a corrected manifest.

`cohort_save()` keeps the logs, but only R reads the rds file.

Proposal: `write_study_yaml()` writes each log as a CSV file next to the manifest, and `read_study_yaml()` reads them back.

title: Record size, modified time and checksum in analysis_files()
description:
`analysis_files()` returns the keys, `path` and `exists`. It does not show whether a result file changed since the last load.

Proposal: add `size` and `modified`, and `sha256` on request.

```r
loaded <- load_analyses(cohort, checksum = TRUE)
names(analysis_files(loaded)$expr)
#> [1] "subject_id" "path" "exists" "size" "modified" "sha256"
```

`fs::file_info()` and `cli::hash_file_sha256()` give these values, and both packages are already imports.

title: Add a sample level to AnalysisSpec
description:
`AnalysisSpec` has the levels `subject`, `pair` and `cohort`. Most pipelines write one file per sample, and a spec cannot describe those files.

```r
analysis_spec_new(
  name = "gene_counts", assay = "bulk_rna", level = "sample",
  path_template = "{root}/{sample_id}.tsv", root_key = "rna_root"
)
#> Error: `level` must be one of: 'subject', 'pair', 'cohort'.
```

With `level = "subject"`, a subject with two samples of one assay loads one file only, and `{sample_id}` is not a known token.

Proposal: a level `sample` with the token `{sample_id}`. It gives one unit per sample of the assay, and the loaded rows get `subject_id` and `sample_id` as keys.

title: Publish a JSON Schema for the study YAML and a specification of the manifest
description:
The format of the study YAML and of the manifest is written in the R help pages only. A Python script or a commit hook cannot check a study file without R.

Proposal: a JSON Schema for the study YAML in `inst/schema/`, and a short specification of the manifest. A test compares the schema with the code, so the two cannot drift.

title: Neutral names for the two sides of a sample pair
description:
`sample_pairs()` pairs any two roles, but its columns are always named for a tumor study.

```r
sample_pairs(sample_map, tumor_role = "day_1", normal_role = "baseline")
#>   subject_id assay    tumor_sample_id normal_sample_id pair_id
#> 1 R1         bulk_rna A2              A1               A2__A1
```

Proposal: `role_a` and `role_b` as arguments, and `sample_id_a` and `sample_id_b` as columns and path tokens. This is in line with `group_a` and `group_b` of `cohort_contrasts()`. The old names keep working for one release.

title: load_analysis() prints the column specification of every file
description:
`load_analysis()` calls `readr::read_csv` and `readr::read_tsv` with their defaults, so every file prints its column specification. Two files give six messages.

```r
loaded <- load_analysis(cohort, spec)
#> Rows: 1 Columns: 2
#> -- Column specification ------------------------------------
#> Delimiter: ","
#> chr (1): gene
#> dbl (1): value
```

Expected: the default readers run with `show_col_types = FALSE` and `progress = FALSE`.

biocohort 0.1.1, R 4.6.1, Windows 11

title: Return every manifest problem as a table
description:
`validate_manifest()` stops at the first kind of problem and shows at most five ids. The error is plain text, so a program cannot read which subject or column is wrong.

```r
manifest <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("R1", "R1", "R2"), species = "human",
  sex = c("F", "M", "M"), assay = "wes",
  sample_id = c("A1", "A2", "A2")
)
validate_manifest(manifest)
#> Error: `manifest` has conflicting subject-level metadata.
#> Subject and column that vary: R1 (sex).
```

The duplicate sample A2 is not reported.

Proposal: `manifest_problems()` runs every check and returns one row per problem, with the subject, the sample and the column.

title: Keep declared contrasts in the cohort and load one result file per contrast
description:
`cohort_contrasts()` lists every pair of subject groups. A study has a short list of comparisons that it chose, each with a name and a direction, and its results are stored per comparison. The cohort has no place for that list.

```r
cohort_contrasts(cohort, by = "group")
#>   group_a group_b   n_a   n_b
#> 1 case    control     1     1

cohort_groups(cohort, by = "role")
#> Error: `by` names column not in `subject_tbl`: role.
```

Proposal: contrasts that are registered in the cohort, on subject or sample columns, and a level `contrast` for one result file per comparison.

```r
cohort <- contrast_register(
  cohort,
  contrast_new(
    id = "case_vs_control", label = "Case against control",
    level = "subject", by = "group", group_a = "case", group_b = "control"
  )
)
contrast_list(cohort)

spec <- analysis_spec_new(
  name = "de_results", assay = "bulk_rna", level = "contrast",
  path_template = "{root}/de/{contrast_id}.tsv", root_key = "rna_root"
)
```

title: Allow a sample id to repeat across assays
description:
`sample_id` must be unique across the whole manifest. Many studies use the same label for the RNA sample and the protein sample of one draw.

```r
manifest <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("R1", "R1"), species = "human",
  assay = c("bulk_rna", "proteomics"), sample_id = c("P01", "P01")
)
validate_manifest(manifest)
#> Error: `manifest` has duplicate samples.
```

`allow_duplicates = TRUE` accepts the manifest. The study YAML round trip then fails, and `join_metadata()` returns two rows for one input row.

Proposal: `validate_manifest(unique_by = c("assay", "sample_id"))`. It accepts a repeat across assays and rejects a repeat inside one assay.

title: Add an extra field for free-form metadata on Study and AnalysisSpec
description:
`Study` and `AnalysisSpec` have fixed fields, and the study YAML rejects any other. A study that reuses public data has no place for the citation and the license.

```yaml
manifest: manifest.csv
study:
  study_id: s
  title: t
  license: CC-BY-4.0
  citation: Author A. Title. 2020.
```

```r
read_study_yaml("study.yaml")
#> Error: unused arguments (license = "CC-BY-4.0", citation = "Author A. Title. 2020.")
```

Proposal: an `extra` field on both classes. It is a named list that the package stores and does not read, and the study YAML keeps it in the round trip.

title: Portable paths in the study YAML: relative paths and environment variables
description:
`write_study_yaml()` writes the paths as they are in memory, which is an absolute path in most cases. The study file then works on one machine only.

```yaml
paths:
  tables: /data/study/tables
```

`read_study_yaml()` also reads no environment variable. It takes `${STUDY_ROOT}/tables` as a folder name.

Proposal: `write_study_yaml(relative = TRUE)` writes each path relative to the study file, and `read_study_yaml()` fills `${NAME}` from the environment.

title: Report ids that differ only by spaces or letter case
description:
`validate_manifest()` keeps each id as it is written, so a space at the end or another letter case makes a new subject. The manifest passes, and one person becomes three.

```r
manifest <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("R1", "R1 ", "r1"),
  species = "human",
  assay = c("WES", "wes", "wes"),
  sample_id = c("A1", "A2", "A3")
)
parsed <- validate_manifest(manifest)
parsed$subject_tbl$subject_id
#> [1] "R1"  "R1 " "r1"
unique(parsed$sample_map$assay)
#> [1] "WES" "wes"
```

`species` is already trimmed and written in lower case.

Proposal: an error for an id with a space at the start or the end, and for two ids that differ only by letter case. `assay` is written in lower case, the same way as `species`.

title: cohort_filter() keeps rows of dropped samples in tables keyed by sample_id
description:
`cohort_filter()` filters a loaded table only when it has a `subject_id` column. A table keyed by `sample_id` keeps the rows of samples that the cohort no longer has.

```r
expr <- data.frame(sample_id = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2"), gene = "G1", value = 1:4)
cohort <- cohort_new(parsed$subject_tbl, parsed$sample_map, analyses = list(expr = expr))

dropped <- cohort_qc(cohort, "B2", scope = "sample", action = "drop", reason = "failed")
samples(dropped)$sample_id
#> [1] "A1" "A2" "B1"
dropped@analyses$expr$sample_id
#> [1] "A1" "A2" "B1" "B2"
```

Expected: a table with a `sample_id` column keeps only the samples that remain.

biocohort 0.1.1, R 4.6.1, Windows 11

title: Warn when a loaded file's key column differs from the unit key
description:
## Description

`load_analysis()` adds the unit keys to every loaded row with `d[[k]] <- u$keys[[k]]`. When the file already has a column with the same name, the file's values are replaced without a message.

## Use Case

A per-sample count file carries its own `sample_id` column, for example the vendor's id `LIB-0042`, while the manifest calls the sample `A1`. After `load_analysis()`, the column holds `A1` and the vendor id is gone. The same happens with `subject_id` at every level and with `pair_id` at the pair level. The package rule is to never change an identifier in silence.

## Proposed Solution

- When a file has a key column and its values differ from the unit key, warn and name the file, the column, and one example of each value.
- Keep the file's column under a new name, such as `file_sample_id`, so nothing is lost.
- A file whose key column already matches the unit key stays as it is, with no warning.

## Alternatives Considered

An error would stop loads that work today for files where the column holds the same id in another spelling. A warning keeps them working and makes the change visible.

title: Generalize manifest layer: species- and assay-agnostic long-format core
description:
## Problem

The manifest layer is hardcoded around a single organism (rat) and two assays (WES, snRNA), which conflicts with the package's stated scope: **any organism (human, mouse, rat, …) and any omics assay (WGS, WES, ATAC-seq, bulk RNA, single-cell, …)**.

Concrete coupling today:

- `validate_manifest()` keys on `rat_id` (**numeric**) and reads named columns `wes_tumor_id`, `wes_normal_id`, `sn_id`. Assay and species are baked into the API.
- It emits per-assay wide tables: `dna_tbl`, `rna_tbl` (and `read_manifest_csv()` emits `wes_pair_tbl`).
- `read_manifest_csv()` no longer delegates to `validate_manifest()` — the two have diverged into separate parsers with incompatible schemas (`subject_id` vs `rat_id`, `wes_*_sample_id` vs `wes_*_id`, `wes_pair_tbl` vs `dna_tbl`).

Adding ATAC-seq / WGS / bulk-RNA under this design means new columns (`atac_id`, `wgs_tumor_id`, …) and new per-assay tables — combinatorial growth.

## Decision

Converge on a single, generic, long-format core:

1. **One subject key:** `subject_id` (character). Drop `rat_id`/numeric keys entirely. Species is a *value* in a `species` column, not part of the key.
2. **One canonical table:** the tidy `sample_map`:
   ```
   subject_id | assay | sample_id | role
   ```
   - `assay` is a free value: `wgs`, `wes`, `atac`, `bulk_rna`, `scrna`, …
   - `role` is a free value: `tumor`, `normal`, … (designs without tumor/normal just use one role)
   - New assays are new **rows**, never new columns or tables.
3. **One parser:** `read_manifest_csv()` delegates to `validate_manifest()` — single validation engine, single source of truth.
4. Per-assay wide views (`dna_tbl`, `wes_pair_tbl`, …) become **derived helpers** computed on demand from `sample_map`, not part of the core return contract.
5. Tumor/normal pairing handled generically (optional pairing key), not WES-specific.

## Why now

Package is v0.2.0, pre-1.0, single developer, no external users. Breaking changes are free now and expensive after 1.0. PR #3 is documentation-heavy with all-new examples on the rat-centric API; fixing the abstraction before merging avoids writing the docs twice.

## Scope of follow-up work

- Refactor `validate_manifest()` to be species- and assay-agnostic (`subject_id` + long `sample_map`).
- Restore `read_manifest_csv()` -> `validate_manifest()` delegation.
- Fix `sample_tbl` inconsistency (currently keeps `rat_id` while all other tables use `subject_id`).
- Update new vignettes (`glossary`, `naming-conventions`) and all examples/`.Rd` to the generic schema.
- NEWS entry as a breaking 0.3.0 change.
